mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors react to the potential economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods with declining GDP, or the correlation between GDP decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production boosts economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same month, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity increase.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals a strong demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased construction activity boosts economic growth and related industries.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the correlation between HOUST increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure in a low-rate environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate potential monetary tightening.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the joint effect of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales (RSAFS) for two consecutive months signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as increased consumer spending boosts corporate earnings and economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of periods with increasing RSAFS, or the correlation between RSAFS increases and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
